verdict.rationale: FireHydrant's own Runbooks attach a Default Runbook to every incident. That runbook always includes an 'Assign a Role' step, which puts the incident opener in the Commander role, and an 'Add Task List' step, so defined roles and task checklists are both first-party capabilities. Depth is thinly evidenced. missing for 10: explicit documentation of additional roles such as comms lead or custom role definitions, detail on task-list contents and tracking, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering leader, incidents carry defined roles (commander, comms lead) and task checklists so response stays coordinated under pressure

citations.quote: **Assign a Role**: Assigns whoever opened the incident to the Commander role.
The default Runbook will always have two default steps: Assign a Role... Add Task List
When you first sign up for an account, FireHydrant builds a Default Runbook for you that always attaches to every incident.
